text:
lina: quick thread: we need guidance on RBAC mapping for migrated keys. current model supports roles: reader, writer, admin scoped to project/org. some legacy keys are used for ad-hoc admin tasks.
derrick: recommendation: don't give admin by default. instead map to the least-privilege role based on historical API calls. e.g., if key only ever called read endpoints -> reader. if it did writes -> writer.
sofia: how precise is our call classification? we have 30 days of logs indexed; we can map endpoints to permission sets with ~95% accuracy but there are noisy endpoints (e.g., /v1/*). propose manual review for any key with mixed activity or any write to billing/admin endpoints.
lina: ok. process: run behavioral classification, auto-assign role_hint, send emails to owners for review if role_hint=admin or ambiguous.
derrick: also flag keys that are used by scheduled jobs (cron metadata) as service tokens and recommend exchange flow.
infra-bot: deploy queued: rbac-migration-feature flag toggles will be added to staging 2026-04-09T02:00Z.
sofia: we should also ensure our SDKs have helper to call exchange endpoint automatically; otherwise adoption will be slow.
lina: good call. add sdk helpers and sample snippets in RFC. derrick: I'll draft the role-mapping SQL & rulebook. sofia: I'll add the SDK snippets.
derrick: timeline: classification run -> 3 days, notifications -> 2 days, manual review window -> 14 days, enforcement -> 60 days.
lina: OK. mark owners and move to tracking.
